1.

This appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act')
has been filed by the claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 23.12.2021 passed by the Basavaraj vs Vijaykumar And Anr on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59976810/
2

Senior Civil Judge & Additional MACT, Basavakalyan, Bidar District (hereinafter NC:
2025:KHC-K:6518-DB HC-KAR referred to as the 'Tribunal' for short) in MVC No.587/2018.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Facts giving rise to the filing of this appeal briefly stated are that, on 09.03.2017 at about 21:30 hrs, the claimant along with his relative namely Ravindrakumar was proceeding on a Suzuki motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-32/W-3257 through Khuba College Road, Basavakalyan.
Ravindrakumar was riding the motorcycle and the claimant was proceeding as a pillion rider.

When they reached near the carving of Akka Nagamma Gavi, at that time, the said Ravindrakumar rode the motorcycle at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life, lost control over the speed of the motorcycle, which skidded.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, the claimant sustained grievous injuries and was hospitalized.
3. The claimant filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation.

It was pleaded that he had NC: 2025:KHC-K:6518-DB HC-KAR spent a huge amount towards medical expenses,
conveyance charges and other incidental costs.
The claimant was hale and healthy at the time of the accident.
He was doing private Electrical work and was earning Rs.600/- per day.
It was further pleaded that the accident occurred purely on account of the rash and negligent riding of the offending motorcycle by its rider.
4. On service of notice, the respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared through their counsel.
Respondent No.1 filed a written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition and stated that the vehicle involved in the accident was fully insured with respondent No.2.

It was further submitted that if the Court comes to the conclusion that the claimant is entitled for any sort of compensation,
the same may be directed to be paid by respondent No.2.
Respondent No.2 filed objections to the main petition, contending that the said accident did not occur due to the rash and negligent act of the rider of the Suzuki Motorcycle.

Instead, it had taken place due to the rider's NC:
2025:KHC-K:6518-DB HC-KAR rash and negligent manner, as he himself dashed against the bridge.
Hence, he prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter recorded the evidence.
The claimant himself was examined as PW.1 and Dr. Rajendra Kothari was examined as PW-2.
The claimant got exhibited documents marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P.95.
Respondent No.2-Insurance Company was examined as RW-1 and did not exhibit any documents.

6. The Claims Tribunal, by the impugned judgment, inter alia, held that the accident took place on account of rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle by its rider, as a result of which, the claimant sustained injuries.

The Tribunal further held that the claimant is entitled to a compensation of Rs.9,44,320/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. and directed the respondent No.2- Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount NC: 2025:KHC-K:6518-DB HC-KAR along with interest.
Being aggrieved, the present appeal has been filed.

7. Smt. Neeva M Chimkod, learned counsel appearing for the claimant has raised the following contentions:

sentences.text: 3 a) Firstly, at the time of the accident, the claimant was earning Rs.18,000/- per month.
But the Tribunal has considered the notional income of the claimant as Rs.9,000/- per month which is on the lower side.
b) Secondly, due to the accident, the claimant has sustained grievous injuries.
He was treated as inpatient for a period of 9 months.

Even after discharge from the hospital,
he was not in a position to discharge his regular work.
He has suffered lot of pain during treatment.
Considering the same, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
The Tribunal has not granted any compensation towards 'loss of income during the laid-up period' and 'loss of amenities'.
Hence, she sought for enhancement of the compensation.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6518-DB HC-KAR 8.

On the other hand, Smt. Preeti Patil Melkundi, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has raised following counter contentions:
a) Firstly, even though the claimant has claimed that he was earning Rs.18,000/- per month, he has not produced any documents to substantiate the same.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly assessed the notional income of the claimant as Rs.9,000/- per month.
b) Secondly, the injuries suffered by the claimant are minor in nature.
Considering the evidence of the doctors and the medical records, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.
Hence, she sought for dismissal of the appeal.

9. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal.
10.

It is not in dispute that the claimant suffered injuries in the road traffic accident that occurred on 09.03.2017 NC: 2025:KHC-K:6518-DB HC-KAR due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing registration no.KA-32/W-3257.
11.
The claimant claims that he was earning Rs.18,000/- per month.
But he has not produced any documents to establish the same.
Therefore, in the absence of proof of income, notional income has to be assessed.

As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, for accidents that occurred in the year 2017, the notional income of the claimant has to be taken as Rs.10,250/- p.m.
12.
As per wound certificate, the claimant has sustained head injury, suffered fits due to collating of blood in the brain.
Taking into consideration the deposition of the doctor and injuries mentioned in the wound certificate, the Tribunal has rightly taken the whole body disability at 37%.

The claimant is aged about 29 years at the time of the accident and multiplier applicable to his age group is '17'.
Basavaraj vs Vijaykumar And Anr on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59976810/
4

Thus, the claimant is entitled for compensation of NC: 2025:KHC-K:6518-DB HC-KAR Rs.7,73,670/- (Rs.10250*12*17*37%) on account of 'loss of future income'.
13.
Due to the accident, the claimant has suffered grievous injuries and also undergone surgery.
He was inpatient in the hospital for a period of nine months.

Considering the prolonged pain during treatment as well as the permanent disability certified by the doctor, we are inclined to enhance the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the head of 'pain and sufferings' from Rs.30,000/- to Rs.80,000/- and the claimant is also entitled for the compensation under the head of 'loss of amenities' Rs.40,000/-.
14.
The nature of injuries indicates that the claimant must have been under rest and treatment for a period of 9 months.

Consequently, the claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.92,250/-
(Rs.10,250*9 months) under the head 'loss of income during laid up period'.
- 10 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:6518-DB HC-KAR 15.
Considering the nature of injuries, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads is just and reasonable.

16. Thus, the claimant is entitled for the following compensation:

5 HC-KAR 17.

sentences.text: In the result, the following order is passed:
ORDER a) The appeal is allowed in part.
b) The judgment of the Claims Tribunal is modified.
c) The claimant is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.12,20,920/-.

d) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount along with interest @ 6%p.a. from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of realization, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment.
- 12 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:6518-DB HC-KAR e) The deposit and release of enhanced compensation shall be as per the order of the Tribunal.
Sd/-
